newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN BLASTS KILLINGS, FORCED RESETTLEMENT IN BURUNDI.
newsitem.headline: UN BLASTS KILLINGS, FORCED RESETTLEMENT IN BURUNDI.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency on Friday condemned the killing of 135 displaced Burundians and a U.N. rights investigator accused authorities in the Central African country of forcing rural poor to resettle "in the vain hope of crushing rebels".

A spokesman for Burundi's military ruler, Pierre Buyoya, said on Thursday that Hutu rebels had killed 135 civilians and wounded about 140 on Wednesday night by shooting them and slashing them with machetes in Cibitoke province.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) reaffirmed that the country was still not safe enough to encourage refugees to return home. Around 300,000 Burundians who fled ethnic killings in 1993 remain abroad -- 260,000 in Tanzania and 40,000 in Zaire.

"We strongly condemn the killing of some 135 displaced Burundians in a regroupment site in Cibitoke province in Burundi," Pamela O'Toole, spokeswoman of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), told a news briefing.

"We believe that the killings demonstrate that the regroupment programme in Burundi does not necessarily provide extra security for returned refugees and the displaced as the government has suggested," she added.
Since November, more than 90,000 Burundi refugees have returned from Zaire. The UNHCR is providing them with aid.
"Although the security situation in some areas of Burundi has improved, we still do not believe it is safe enough to encourage refugees to return to the country," O'Toole said.
Paulo Sergio Pinheiro, a Brazilian lawyer who serves as U.N. special rapporteur (investigator) on Burundi, issued a report on Friday condemning the forced resettlement of rural poor.

"While maintaining a war mentality in the vain hope of crushing the rebels in the field...the Burundi de facto authorities are systematically resettling rural populations using an outdated strategy of forced villagisation..." Pinheiro wrote in his report to the U.N. Human Rights Commission.

"The Special Rapporteur vigorously disapproves of and condemns the forced resettlement of rural populations as a manifest violation of the relevant provisions of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights...to which Burundi is a party," he added.
